svg.aria-label: Diagram: A CloudWatch Logs field index enables efficient equality-based searches, and when a query uses one it attempts to skip processing log events known not to include the indexed field, which reduces the scan volume that Logs Insights queries are billed on under the DataScanned-Bytes usage type. The index is a property of ingestion rather than of a log group: CloudWatch Logs indexes only the log events ingested after an index policy is created and does not index events ingested before, and each matching event remains indexed for 30 days from its ingestion time, while log group retention is independent and may be much longer, so one log group holds three zones of events decided by arrival time. An index created during an incident therefore does nothing for that incident. The filterIndex command returns indexed data only, forcing a query to scan only log groups indexed on the specified field, and for each indexed log group it attempts to scan only events that have the indexed field and also returns only results from after the field index was created, so two exclusions are applied silently and the command reports neither. Using filter instead scans the un-indexed log groups too, every event in them, which costs more and is complete. Four conditions make an index silently inapplicable with no error: indexed fields are case-sensitive so RequestId does not match requestId, field indexes are supported only for the structured log formats of JSON and service logs, the index serves equality searches of the form field equals value or field IN a list, and the skip applies to values CloudWatch Logs has detected for that field in the past. Quotas are 20 fields per policy, 100 characters per field name, and as many as 40 account-level index policies of which 20 may use log group name prefix selection criteria and 20 may use data source based selection criteria, with no two prefix policies allowed to overlap. A log-group-level policy overrides account-level policies that match the log group as a whole, replacing rather than adding to them, while account-level policies matching at the log event level for a data source name and type apply in addition. A filterIndex query can scan as many as 10,000 log groups chosen by as many as five log group name prefixes. Default field indexes exist for all Standard log class log groups and for CloudTrail, VPC flow log and WAF data sources, and they do not count towards the quota. A field index policy created in a monitoring account is not used for log groups in linked source accounts, because a policy applies only in the account where it is created.
svg.title: A field index is a property of ingestion time, not of a log group
svg.text: An index is not an attribute of the log group. It is a window over arrivals.
“CloudWatch Logs indexes only the log events ingested after an index policy is created.” And: “each matching
log event remains indexed for 30 days from the log event’s ingestion time.”
One log group, three zones — decided entirely by when each event arrived
before the policy not indexed, and never will be
after it, within 30 days indexed — the only zone an index can accelerate
after it, beyond 30 days fallen out of the index; retention is unaffected
So an index created during an incident does nothing for that incident. Create policies with the log group.
filterIndex changes the answer, not only the cost
“… it attempts to scan only log events that have the indexed field, and it also returns only results from
after the field index was created.”
filterIndex skips un-indexed log groups entirely + drops pre-index events
filter scans them, every event — costs more, and is complete
Both exclusions are silent. No state, no warning, no flag. Just fewer rows that look like an answer.
FOUR SILENT NON-USES
case — “RequestId won’t match … requestId”
format — “only … JSON and service logs”
shape — equality or IN, nothing else
value — one it has “detected … in the past”
None errors. The only symptom is the bill.
QUOTAS AND PRECEDENCE
20 fields/policy 100 chars/field name
40 account policies = 20 prefix + 20 data source
filterIndex reach: 10,000 log groups, 5 prefixes
A log-group policy REPLACES account policies that
match the group; data-source ones still apply.
Check the free defaults before writing any policy
CloudTrail: eventSource, eventName, errorCode, readOnly, requestId · VPC flow: action, logStatus, region
WAF: action, httpRequest.country · all Standard-class groups: @logStream, traceId, severityText — quota-free.
And the cross-account inversion: “If you create a field index policy in a monitoring account, that policy is not
used for log groups in linked source accounts.” The wide queries run where the policy has no effect.
Indexes are a cost control and a speed control. They are not a completeness guarantee.
